base_properties.human_readable: The Kirby-Paris Theorem (Independence of Goodstein's Theorem)

perspectives.label: The Unprovable Statement
perspectives.comment: From the perspective of a statement unprovable within PA, it's a mountain: an immutable limit of the formal system. No escape.

perspectives.label: The Analytical Observer
perspectives.comment: The analytical observer, understanding the theorem, sees an inherent limitation of Peano Arithmetic. It's a mountain due to the inherent nature of the system.

commentary.narrative_context: The Kirby-Paris theorem demonstrates that Goodstein's theorem—a true statement about the termination of specific sequences of natural numbers—is unprovable within Peano Arithmetic (PA). This highlights an inherent limitation in the power of formal systems to prove all true statements, making it a fundamental concept in mathematical logic.
key_agents: The Unprovable Statement: A mathematical statement that is true but cannot be proven within Peano Arithmetic (powerless/trapped)
The Analytical Observer: A mathematician or logician who understands the implications of the theorem (analytical/analytical)
commentary.logic_rationale: The extractiveness is low because the theorem doesn't actively extract from anything; it reveals a limitation. Suppression is low as well. The theorem doesn't suppress other theorems, it just shows what PA can't prove. Theater ratio is essentially nonexistent.
commentary.perspectival_gap: Since this is a mountain classification, all perspectives are in agreement.
